To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Bjorken solution is a special case of a more general class of self-similar solutions of relativistic fluid dynamics; (2) these solutions can describe longitudinally and cylidrically expanding systems with inhomogeneous rapidities; and (3) the solutions are simple enough to allow analytic calculations of the energy spectra of the produced particles and of their azimuthal correlations.

(1) the Hwa– Bjorken solution of relativistic hydrodynamic equations is a special case of more general solutions, and (2) the general solutions can be obtained in closed analytic form, and are simple enough that their properties are easily understood.

the longitudinal expansion of a hot and dense medium produced by the collision of two heavy ions at high energy can be described by a relativistic hydrodynamical solution with an inhomogeneous rapidiy distribution, which is self-similar in space and time, and that this solution can also be extended to a cylindrically symmetrized version, corresponding to central heavy ion collisions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of simple, self-similar solutions of relativistic fluid dynamics, which may be used for the analysis of experimental data from relativistic heavy ion collisions.
the development of simple, self-similar analytic solutions of relativistic fluid dynamics, which may be useful in understanding the physics of high energy collisions.

the following topics: i) The construction of a relativistic hydrodynamic model of a longitudinally and cylidrically expanding firetube, ii) The construction of analytic, self-similar solutions of the hydrodynamic equations, iii) The application of these solutions to the description of the evolution of the system created in heavy ion collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrodynamics is a very useful tool to describe the evolution of a system of particles in a relativistic regime.

the Hwa– Bjorken solution of (1+3)D relativistic hydrodynamcis, as well as its generalizations, are not valid for central collisions of heavy nuclei at RHIC energies, because the initial energy density in the firetubes is too low.

the simple analytic solutions of (i) Bjorken, (ii) Hwa–Barkai, and (iii) the generalized solutions presented in this paper provide an excellent description of the longitudinal evolution of the expanding system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Bjorken boost-invariance is the most simple and most important solution for (1+1)D relativistic hydrodynamical systems, but for (1+3)D relativistic cylindrically symmetrical systems the Bjorken solution is only a special case, and there is a large class of other solutions which can be more realistic.

, in the framework of the hydrodynamics, there exist simple, analytic solutions, describing the space-time evolution of the matter produced in heavy-ion collisions, in a wide range of bombarding energies.

the solutions presented here are the relativistic generalizations of the well-known solutions of non-relativistic hydrodynamics, which are widely used to describe the dynamics and evolution of the matter created in heavy ion collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the case of a cylindrically and longitudinally expanding firetube, the transverse flow velocity profile is independent of the rapidity distribution, and that the rapidity distribution is independent of the transverse profile.

the longitudinal expansion of the matter produced in such collisions can be treated analytically, and that the resulting analytic expressions for the space–time evolution of the matter are very simple.

, for the case of central collisions, a simple analytic solution exists for a cylindrically expanded fireball, with a constant energy per baryon, and a longitudinal expansion with an arbitrary rapidity dependence.
